note: On the criteria as written he is a core fit, and that is precisely the finding. Successful: owns a distribution company importing from China and selling wholesale, after a career as a restaurateur. Income: the business is doing very well and he absorbed $6,000 and $9,000 without resistance — his personal liquidity is nil post-divorce, but corporate funds are real funds and he asked how to pay, not whether he could. Good-to-great is close to verbatim: 'I'm in a very good place right now. I would like to get better... I would like to get a lot more aesthetically defined... I'm hitting a bit of a plateau.' Not deconditioned: trains six days a week from 5:30am. He misses only on neglected health, and he misses it in the opposite direction from most — his health is not neglected, it has dominated his life. Which is the point. This man had four abdominal surgeries, six weeks in hospital and three weeks on a ventilator five months before this call, plus a colectomy at 23 and brain damage at 18, and the stated ICP scores him as an ideal customer because it screens on occupation, income and starting point and has no clinical criterion whatsoever. He is the clearest evidence in the corpus that the ICP as stated cannot distinguish a good customer from a person who should not be sold loaded ballistic training without a surgeon's sign-off.
